If you're like me, you've probably spent time on Wikipedia just clicking around, randomly browsing different articles. Now there's finally an official app for that — though honestly, it's just a little tool for you to do exactly that.

Now there's finally one more button that can take you directly to a random Wikipedia article.

Today's update to the Wikipedia iOS app has added a fun and practical new feature: a "Random Article" widget that can be placed on the home screen of your iPhone or iPad.

This widget comes in both large and medium sizes, and even has a cute mascot.

Tap the widget once and it'll take you to a completely random Wikipedia article, opening it in random mode.

You don't need to exit the app and tap the widget again — just tap the "Random" button to keep rolling the dice, going deeper and deeper into this random maze.

Have fun, but be careful not to lose track of time. Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app also added a history trivia mini-game.

After you update the Wikipedia app on your iPhone and iPad today, you'll be able to find this brand-new widget.

Enjoy your Apple device to the fullest!
